about: Round 17 (guns, G3): source material for the gun families in LAYERS, for a full-range living-room system that still reads on a laptop. Each source is one layer of a shot - the crack, the body, the mechanism, the tail - and tools/audio/gun_layers.py composes directions from them (with a synthesised pressure-front crack and a sub that ElevenLabs does not make). Prompts describe the physical event and where the microphone is, never 'a big gun' (round 5: prompting the object returns the cliche). Spend authorised by the lead's words for round 17 (C17.5); every run on ledger.md. Generate: python3 tools/audio/sfx_generate.py --approved --sources assets/audio/elevenlabs/guns_r17.json [--only id].

sources.prompt: A 120 mm smoothbore tank main gun firing, recorded in open ground 50 metres to the side: a violent supersonic crack with an instant attack, then a massive concussive boom you feel in the chest as the pressure wave hits, loose metal rattling, then a long rolling echo across the terrain. One single shot, no music.

A battle tank firing its main gun, recorded 300 metres away across a wide valley: the sharp sonic crack arrives first, then the deep heavy boom, then thunderous echoes rolling back off the hills for several seconds. One single shot, no music.
Only the echo after a huge cannon shot, without the shot itself: a deep rumbling thunder rolling back off distant hills and concrete walls, wide and spacious, slowly fading out over several seconds.
Inside a tank turret right after the main gun fires: the heavy steel breech block slamming open and a spent cartridge stub ejecting and clanging onto the steel floor. Close microphone, no gunshot.
A single extremely sharp supersonic muzzle blast recorded very close: one violent broadband crack like a giant whip snapping, an instant attack and almost no decay, no echo, no boom.

Exactly one round fired from a 25 mm chain gun on an armoured fighting vehicle, recorded 30 metres away outdoors: a hard heavy report with a sharp supersonic crack and a deep punchy thump, a short slap echo. One single shot.

A Bradley fighting vehicle's 25 mm chain gun firing a short controlled burst of four rounds, each round a separate heavy cracking report with a deep thump, a slow deliberate rhythm, recorded 40 metres away outdoors with echoes off concrete.

An attack helicopter's 30 mm chain gun firing a short burst, recorded 50 metres away: a fast hammering string of heavy cannon reports, each one a hard crack and a deep punch, the chain drive clattering, then the echo rolling away.

Very close recording of a chain gun's mechanism cycling once, without the gunshot: the chain drive clacking, the heavy bolt slamming home, belt links and a large brass casing clinking onto a steel deck.

A .50 calibre heavy machine gun firing one long continuous burst, recorded 20 metres to the side outdoors: every round a deep powerful thumping report with a sharp crack, a heavy steady cyclic rate, the receiver hammering, brass and links clinking, slap echoes off concrete. No pauses.
Exactly one shot from a .50 calibre heavy machine gun recorded 20 metres away: a deep powerful report with a sharp crack and a short echo. One single shot.

Close recording of a heavy machine gun's receiver working without the gunshots: the bolt hammering back and forth at a steady rate, the ammunition belt rattling through, brass casings tinkling onto a steel deck.

An armoured vehicle exploding as its ammunition detonates, recorded 60 metres away: a violent sharp blast crack, a deep roaring fireball that hits the chest, heavy metal debris raining down and clattering, small secondary pops, then a long rumbling echo.
After an explosion: heavy chunks of steel and burning fragments raining down onto concrete and metal, clattering and bouncing, crackling flames, no explosion.
Only the deep rumbling aftershock of a massive explosion rolling around a huge concrete stadium, without the blast itself: a long wide thunder slowly dying away.

A tank shell exploding against a reinforced concrete wall, recorded 40 metres away: a violent sharp crack, chunks of concrete blasting off and raining down onto the ground, a cloud of grit. One single impact.

A high-explosive tank shell striking the side of a steel shipping container, recorded 40 metres away: a huge metallic boom and clang, the container's thin steel walls booming and ringing, shrapnel rattling. One single impact.
A large shell exploding in shallow water, recorded 50 metres away: a deep heavy thump, a tall geyser of water erupting and then crashing and splashing back down. One single impact.
Exactly one 25 mm high-explosive cannon round bursting in dry packed earth, recorded 30 metres away: a sharp crack and a solid thump, dirt and gravel spraying. One single impact.
Exactly one 25 mm cannon round hitting a concrete wall, recorded 30 metres away: a sharp explosive crack, chips of concrete and dust spraying off. One single impact.
Exactly one 25 mm cannon round hitting thick steel plate, recorded 20 metres away: a hard metallic bang with a short ringing clang. One single impact.

Exactly one 25 mm armour-piercing round slamming into the side of an armoured vehicle, recorded 20 metres away: a heavy metallic bang and a deep hollow clang ringing inside the hull. One single impact.
Exactly one heavy machine-gun bullet striking dry dirt and gravel close by: a short sharp thud and a spray of grit. One single impact.
Exactly one heavy machine-gun bullet striking a concrete wall close by: a sharp crack and chips of concrete flying. One single impact.
Exactly one bullet striking the surface of water close by: a sharp short slap and splash. One single impact.
The sharp supersonic snap of a heavy machine-gun bullet passing very close by, a whip-like crack and a tiny hiss, no gunshot.
